This is the second creation from Kakashii.tez!

These pieces were generated all through javascript code and allow the user to interact with their token using the WASD or arrow keys to move around the maze however they want!

These pieces have four different features attached to them:
- Size: The size of the maze. (Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, GIGANTIC)
- Footprints: If true, enables the user to produce footprints when moving through the maze.
- Teleport: If true, enables the user to teleport randomly in the maze using the "T" key.
- Wallhacks: If true, enables the user to be able to run through any and all walls of the maze.

I hope you all enjoy minting your very own maze, hope the hash rarities are on your side, and above all; have fun in the Maze Runner!

Interaction Notes:
- Use "W" or up arrow to move up.
- Use "A" or left arrow to move left.
- Use "S" or down arrow to move down.
- Use "D" or right arrow to move right.
- If you have the teleport feature, use "T" to teleport at any time.

4776.d:
Currency 1.0

This is one of a series of conceptual artworks about art and valuation. Each artwork is an exact replica of itself, so all the generative pieces look and feel the same. This work references Fxhash & Tezos eco-system and thus each token is fictionally named as FXT, but it has no relation to the official platforms. 

This artwork attempts to questions the basic premise of art valuation - does art have any value if the art itself costs nothing? Is the value of art what the anyone wants to pay for the work? Is art itself the currency, or is currency the art?

There are 2500 editions in Currency 1.0, with each edition costing 0 XTZ. 
Royalty is 10%, the minimum permitted.

Currency 1.0 @beardcoded

4815.d:
Industrial design has taken many forms in the past decades, and some of them have endured. The manual of mass-produced technical products have kept on featuring pseudo-technical diagrams of your most recent purchase. But for now, you will ignore it and assume that its use will be intuitive enough for you to manage. Only when you have a problem with it will you explore this little piece of literature, and discover that you've been doing it wrong all along.

This moka piece is a mix of different cultural perspectives on the service manual exercise. The moka pot's European orientalist origin is blended with the idiomatic Swedish brand naming shenanigans and the 80s Japanese service manual schematics aesthetics.

w=stat(6)s=1

cls()pal({-8,8,9,10,11,12,-4,0,-8,8,9,10,11,12,-4},1)r=rnd

::_::goto _

Inspired by how different ideas lead to new ideas, the same basic discoveries growing exponentially into a wild network of connected concepts and ways of understand reality.

"Overgrown Monoliths" is the result of an algorithm that started in April 2021. It was called "Grass.js".
Spring was blooming all around the house, taking over the stones and remnants of ancient battles that stood here. Inspiration was everywhere.
The initial goal was to use mathematical formulas for creating patterns inspired by the density of nature, that could be used by a pen plotter, so it kept focusing on outputting vector lines. This history and practice produced a graphical style based on line strokes, plus occasionally some transparent, filled shapes.
Each artwork will be either Garden or Monolith, for they are variations of two existing pieces from my workshop.
Each generative image allows for downloading a SVG file of the line art, ready for plotters -> just press 's' key in live mode when the computing has completed.
The "Format" feature tells you what machine size and paper size you would need, if you were willing to give it a try. A warning though, some of the SVGs can be tricky, servo-killers.

NOTE: this is completely procedural and while I do my best to shape the possibility space such that you get interesting and beautiful variety, it can happen that something 'broken' shows up. If you get a completely solid colored screen then shoot me a DM on twitter and I'll happily send you something else.

Moiré pattern is a geometrical design created by superposing set of lines to another set. The pattern can be found in our daily lives such as LCD monitor screens and screen windows. 

studio2009 created the pattern by overlapping two sets of polygons created with multiple lines. To add some variations, we have added color ways, rotation, and distortion which can be found in features. The distortion in particular are available in three different modes: simple, exponential, and tangential. Please enjoy.
